finding.claim: Sync verifier created with key '' or null accepts unsigned tokens when algorithms includes an alg (read-only analysis; not executed).
finding.source: Token string: attacker chooses alg and omits the signature segment.
finding.sink: Signature verification skipped in validateAlgorithmAndSignature; claims returned as trusted.

trace.note: keyType check accepts 'string' and 'object' (null), so '' and null pass.

'if (key && keyType !== "function")' is false for '' and null, so detectPublicKeyAlgorithms and prepareKeyOrSecret never run; the empty-key check in prepareKeyOrSecret is skipped, unlike the async path.
Empty signature segment matches /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]*$/ and is accepted.
hasKey = !!key is false, so neither the missingSignature (274) nor missingKey (276) branch fires.
alg is in the configured allowlist (attacker's HS256 is allowed by config).
'if (signature && ...)' is skipped because signature is ''.
Validators pass for a token without exp, and the payload is returned.

finding.guards_checked: Base64url regex (decoder.js:10,41-43); alg allowlist (verifier.js:162), which passes by config; hasKey && !signature guard (verifier.js:274), gated on a truthy key; empty-key check (verifier.js:38), which the sync path bypasses. Precondition: key is '' or null AND algorithms is non-empty. Empty algorithms list rejects all algs, so not affected.

finding.claim: Cached success result for a token without iat ignores exp, so an expired token is accepted from the cache for up to cacheTTL (default 600000 ms) after exp (read-only analysis; not executed).
finding.source: Token with exp but no numeric iat, first presented while still valid; replayed later.
finding.sink: Cache-hit return path in verify() (verifier.js:364-378), which skips validators.

trace.note: hasIat = typeof payload.iat === 'number' is false, so the block at 119-129 is skipped and cacheValue[2] stays 0 (exp not read).
maxTTL = clockTimestamp + clockTolerance + cacheTTL.
cacheValue[2] = maxTTL because it was 0.
Cache lookup on later request; min === 0 and now <= max, so the stored payload is returned.
exp validator (304-323) is never run on the cache-hit path.

finding.guards_checked: exp validator runs only on cache miss (verifier.js:304-323); cacheTTL clamp (verifier.js:134) bounds the window but does not enforce exp; signature check ran once at cache-store time. Precondition: cache enabled (createCache, verifier.js:84-85) and token lacks numeric iat (e.g. signer noTimestamp or external issuer).

finding.claim: maxAge is silently not enforced for tokens without an iat claim (fail-open; read-only analysis; not executed).
finding.source: Validly signed token with no iat claim.
finding.sink: Freshness check implemented by the iat date validator pushed when maxAge is set.

trace.note: maxAge number pushes an iat date validator (616-618).
'if (!(claim in payload)) continue' skips the validator when iat is absent.
cacheSet also ignores maxAge when iat is absent (126-127 are inside the hasIat block).

finding.guards_checked: requiredClaims (verifier.js:293-299) blocks such tokens only if the app lists iat there; signature check passes for legitimately issued tokens. Precondition: maxAge configured, iat not in requiredClaims, issuer omits iat.

finding.claim: Signature segment accepts non-canonical base64url trailing bits, so one signature has several token-string encodings; string-keyed revocation or replay checks can be bypassed (read-only analysis; not executed).
finding.source: Signature segment of a valid token, re-encoded by changing unused trailing bits of its last character.
finding.sink: Application revocation, one-time-use, or replay check keyed on the raw token string; cache keys (utils.js:45-58) also differ per variant.

trace.note: Only the alphabet is checked, not canonical form.
Buffer.from(signature, 'base64') ignores unused trailing bits, so decoded bytes are unchanged.
Same bytes verify, so each variant passes (HS256 gives 4 variants).
Cache key hashes the full string, so each variant gets its own cache entry.

finding.guards_checked: Base64url alphabet check (decoder.js:10); signing input header.payload is not malleable because it is used verbatim; HMAC/RSA verification itself is correct. Precondition: app identifies tokens by raw string.

finding.claim: With caching enabled, a token passed as a Buffer makes verify() throw TypeError before decoding (availability bug; read-only analysis; not executed).
finding.source: Token passed as a Buffer (for example from a body parser).
finding.sink: cacheKeyBuilder(token) called on the raw Buffer before the Buffer-to-string conversion; throws synchronously, even in callback/async mode.

trace.note: Type check accepts Buffer as a valid token type.
cacheKeyBuilder(token) is called before decode converts the Buffer.
token.split('.', 1) is not a method on Buffer, so TypeError is thrown.
Buffer-to-string conversion happens only later, inside decode, which is never reached.

finding.guards_checked: Type check at verifier.js:353 (passes for Buffer); cache lookup is not guarded. Fail-closed: no bypass, only an error.
